title.narrative: Provision of life-saving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) supplies and services in the communities and shelters affected by Hurricane Beryl in Grenada and St. Vincent and the Grenadines

description.narrative: Hurricane Beryl's impact has been devastating for entire communities within Grenada and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and important efforts are needed to reach all the children and their families in need to ensure their access to WASH life-saving services and practices. The project aims to support the recovery of critical WASH services in communities and public institutions (shelters) and to enable WASH life-saving practices at most affected household and communities. CERF’s contribution will support ensuring access to humanitarian WASH services to affected population through solutions preventing risk of water borne diseases and responding especially to women and girl’s needs consistent with the WASH Core Commitments for Children in Emergencies. Key priorities will be: 1) to support WASH practice at household level with WASH hygiene supplies and risk communication and community engagement; 2) to support the provision of life-saving WASH services at community and shelter levels. UNICEF will support life-saving WASH services, including the provision of safe water, water quality monitoring and improvement of WASH practices at communities through key WASH supplies and risk communication and community engagement. The priority will be to ensure minimum humanitarian WASH standards in shelters and surrounding affected homes, including a gender focus and AAP. All will be coordinated in the field with relevant sectors as shelters, protection and GBV, enhancing a multisector response for affected populations. Additionally, activities will be implemented in close coordination with the Child Protection team to ensure coherent approaches to affected population in and outside of shelters. Hygiene kits will need to be procured and distributed to vulnerable households to also prevent disease spread as well as ensuring timely access to culturally appropriate, gender and age sensitive information, services and interventions related to hygiene promotion and adopting safe hygiene practices. Lack of access to safe water, handwashing with soap and sanitation facilities will most likely trigger an even worse scenario of water borne related diseases that disproportionally affect children under 5 years old, undermining their capacity to thrive in life as well as other already vulnerable groups
